title: Bad Deployment — v1.8.2 N+1 Regression
description: order-service:v1.8.2 is deployed over the stable v1.8.1. The new build contains an N+1 query regression in the order-listing endpoint, so DB queries per request explode immediately after the deploy timestamp. The deployments table is the audit trail that ties the regression to a specific release.

true_root_cause.summary: Deployment order-service@v1.8.2 (commit 62f544cf…) introduced a missing eager-load in list_orders() — the ORM fetches order items in a separate SELECT per order (N+1 anti-pattern)

key_evidence_signals.expected_behaviour: New row: order-service@v1.8.2 deployed by ci-pipeline shortly after order-service@v1.8.1; incident start aligns with this timestamp
Ratio jumps from ~2 to ~22 for default page_size=20 immediately after the v1.8.2 deploy timestamp
p95 rises after the deploy — latency regression starts at the deploy boundary, not before
Remains near zero — the regression causes slowness, not failures
Each individual query is fast — the DB itself is healthy; only the query COUNT grew

red_herrings: The deploy is the trigger, but blaming 'the deployment' alone is incomplete — the agent must show WHY (query-count ratio) that the deploy is guilty
Elevated latency could be misread as DB slowness — but db_query_duration_seconds p95 and the query-count-per-request signals rule out a slow DB
CPU may rise slightly from SQLAlchemy object hydration — not the root cause
recommended_fix: Rollback order-service to v1.8.1 (known-good), then fix the N+1 with joinedload/selectinload before re-deploying
evaluation_checks: Agent reads the deployments table and identifies v1.8.2 as the change that correlates with incident start
Agent cites db_queries_total ratio jump as the evidence that connects the deploy to the regression
Agent recommends rollback to v1.8.1 as the immediate mitigation
Agent does NOT blame the database itself (individual query latency is stable)
